_doc: Coding-effort engine (v4). Hours are developer hours for CODE and SQL work only: porting projects, fixing findings, converting database code and data access. QA, DevOps / infrastructure, project management, parallel-development drift and contingency are deliberately NOT estimated. Every number is a [low, high] range of manual-equivalent hours with its mode at low + likely_position x (high - low); totals are rolled up by Monte Carlo ("rollup"): the range is P10-P90, 'likely' is P50 and P80 is the commitment figure. Calibration anchor: AWS reported 143,000 lines of .NET Framework ported with about 270 developer hours saved (about 1.9 manual hours per KLOC for a clean mechanical port, AWS Transform for .NET case study, Caribbean Examinations Council); human-designed work (UI rewrite, auth, interop) is far slower, hence the higher rates for those project types. Recalibrate from your own actuals here, never in code. See references/estimation-model.md.

rollup._doc: Monte Carlo roll-up (_montecarlo.py). Adding every item's low and every item's high assumes all items land at the same extreme together; that range widens with every item and the AI factors stack on top (v5 gave a 4x spread). Industry practice sums expectations and combines spreads: each item is a triangular three-point estimate (low, mode at likely_position, high); items share one driver with correlation 'correlation' (0.3 = the default of the DoD / NASA Joint Agency Cost and Schedule Risk Handbook, cited in GAO-20-195G); the AI factors are systemic (one draw per iteration for every item, mode at factor_position of their range). Reported: P10-P90 range (the 80% interval AACE 18R-97 uses), P50 likely, P80 commitment; the old sums stay as bounds_hours. Fixed seed: reruns give the same numbers.
rollup.label: P10-P90

scale._doc: Diseconomy of scale (COCOMO II: effort grows as size^B with B about 1.10). Project conversion hours in a repository are multiplied by max(1, (repository hand-written KLOC / reference_kloc) ^ exponent): a 360 KLOC repository pays about 1.4x per KLOC what a 10 KLOC one pays. Repositories of at least large_kloc also put 'likely' at likely_position_large instead of likely_position. Evidence: references/estimation-validation.md (the Smartstore port).

ai_assistance._doc: Share of manual-equivalent effort that remains when coding agents / AWS Transform for .NET / GitHub Copilot app modernization do the mechanical part and engineers direct, review and fix. AWS cites up to 4x faster on mechanical porting (factor 0.25) and about 47% overall productivity gain; the range below sits between the two because findings and rewrites stay human. db: AWS DMS Schema Conversion (generative AI) converts most T-SQL, the rest is review. Set enabled=false for a manual-only estimate.
ai_assistance._doc_redesign: redesign_factor applies instead of code_factor / db_factor to work with no mechanical path: Web Forms projects (UI rewrite), findings whose effort key is in redesign_effort_keys, database constructs and findings at the 'redesign' level, and the dual-database abstraction. Published AI gains (AWS Transform 47-70 %, Google >= 50 %) are for mechanical transformation; the METR 2025 trial found experienced developers 19 % slower on open-ended work (references/estimation-validation.md).

conversion_hours_per_kloc._doc: Manual-equivalent hours per 1,000 hand-written C# / VB lines to port a project to SDK-style and the target .NET (generated code excluded). Markup has its own rate.

conversion_fixed_hours._doc: Manual-equivalent hours per project that do not scale with lines: project file, package set, build break-fix.

markup_hours_per_kloc._doc: Views and pages (cshtml, aspx, ascx, master, xaml): far less change than C# when the UI stack stays; Web Forms markup is rewritten.

complexity._doc: Multiplier on a project's conversion hours (not on finding hours, which already count the hard parts). Decision density = decision points per KLOC of hand-written code (_complexity.py). Band limits are upper bounds. Projects under min_kloc are not scaled, because density of a handful of lines is noise. Fan-in: a project many others depend on needs more care. Big files: files over 800 lines are slower to read and port. Result is clamped to [min, max]. Run-time indirection (map_graphs.py wiring, from the codebase-documenter C# resolver): calls bound at run time per KLOC (DI dispatch to an implementation, decorators, overrides, keyed services, MediatR / bus messages, events, method groups, stored delegates, background jobs, redirects, filters, service-locator calls). These are the calls an engineer cannot follow by reading the code, so porting and testing them is slower; the extra is added before the clamp. Reflection sites add a small extra each (capped). The registrations themselves are costed as di-wiring findings, not here.

finding_hours._doc: Manual-equivalent remediation hours per finding: fixed + per extra occurrence, capped. Findings marked baseline are already inside the conversion rate and add nothing. Database effort keys (db-object-*) are only charged in a database scenario.

other_r_hours._doc: Code and configuration work for applications that are not ported: retire, repurchase (integration code only), retain on Windows (repoint connection strings and endpoints), desktop client (repoint service endpoints).

hosting_scenarios._doc: Code-side scenario. modernize: port to .NET 10 for Linux (per-application 7R decisions, Windows-bound parts replaced). windows-rehost: lift-and-shift the existing Windows app to EC2 Windows, only code / configuration that must change for the new network and identity (keep_categories). skip_categories: findings not needed in a scenario.

modernize.label: Convert .NET Windows applications to .NET 10 on Linux

windows-rehost.label: Lift-and-shift Windows applications from on-premises to Windows EC2 (no code port)

database_scenarios._doc: Database code scenario. Only the code and SQL conversion is costed (objects, data-access code, provider abstraction); data migration, tooling set-up and database testing are not.
database_scenarios.dual: Dual support: the application runs on both SQL Server and PostgreSQL
database_scenarios.postgresql: PostgreSQL only: schema, T-SQL code and data access converted, SQL Server removed
database_scenarios.none: Keep SQL Server: no database code change

postgres._doc: Manual-equivalent hours to convert SQL Server objects and data-access code to PostgreSQL (before db_factor). Routine size: small <= 50 lines, medium <= 200, large above. AWS DMS Schema Conversion automates most table and simple routine conversion, so table and view hours are low; the hours are the review and the hand-rewrite of complex routines.

dual.note: Both providers must stay in sync: provider-neutral data access (EF Core with provider-specific migrations, no T-SQL in application code), every procedure maintained for both engines or moved into the application.

postgres._doc_code_hours: inline_sql_strings = parsed SQL statements embedded in C#; tsql_in_strings = those using constructs that need a rewrite or redesign; dynamic_sql_in_code = statements built at run time (holes / concatenated expressions / sp_executesql), reviewed by hand.

team._doc: Default team for the coding timeline.

timeline._doc: Coding timeline only: waves of applications after the shared libraries, database code in parallel with the last waves. Wave overlap lets the next wave start before the previous one ends.

sprints._doc: Coding sprint plan (estimate_effort.py sprint_plan). Sprint 1 starts on the day the team gets codebase access (assessment.json scenario.start_date or --start-date; without a date the plan counts weeks). Capacity per sprint = engineers x days_per_week x length_weeks x hours_per_day x team.efficiency; work is planned at P50 and listed in dependency order: shared libraries, then application waves, with database code in its own lane (db_engineers) when the scenario changes database code. onboarding_days at the start of Sprint 1 cover clone, restore, baseline build and the existing tests on the current stack: calendar time only, not in the coding estimate.

activity_thresholds._doc: Commits per week over the git activity window that mark a repository active or hot (parallel-development risk in scan_repo.py).

complexity_bands._doc: Work-package size label from likely person-days.
